title: Code of Practice for General-Purpose AI Models: Copyright Chapter

policy_extraction.issuing_body: European Commission (AI Office) / General-Purpose AI Code of Practice Working Group 1
covered_actors: Signatories providing or controlling online search engines
prohibited_practices: Circumventing effective technological measures (such as subscription models or paywalls) designed to prevent or restrict unauthorised access when web-crawling for text and data mining and GPAI model training
Web-crawling websites recognised by EU/EEA courts or public authorities as persistently and repeatedly infringing copyright and related rights on a commercial scale
Copyright-infringing uses of general-purpose AI models (to be prohibited in Signatories' acceptable use policies, terms and conditions, or open-source model documentation)

evidence.quote:
Signatories commit:
a) not to circumvent effective technological measures as defined in Article 6(3) of Directive 2001/29/EC that are designed to prevent or restrict unauthorised acts in respect of works and other protected subject matter, in particular by respecting any technological denial or restriction of access imposed by subscription models or paywalls

Signatories commit:
a) to employ web-crawlers that read and follow instructions expressed in accordance with the Robot Exclusion Protocol (robots.txt), as specified in the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) Request for Comments No. 9309

Signatories commit to take appropriate measures to enable affected rightsholders to obtain information about the web crawlers employed, their robots.txt features and other measures that a Signatory adopts to identify and comply with rights reservations expressed pursuant to Article 4(3) of Directive (EU) 2019/790 at the time of crawling by making public such information
Signatories commit to designate a point of contact for electronic communication with affected rightsholders and provide easily accessible information about it.

Signatories will draw up, keep up-to-date and implement a policy to comply with Union law on copyright and related rights for all general-purpose AI models they place on the Union market. Signatories commit to describe that policy in a single document incorporating the Measures set out in this Chapter.

in case of general-purpose AI models released under free and open source licenses to alert users to the prohibition of copyright infringing uses of the model in the documentation accompanying the model without prejudice to the free and open source nature of the license.

To serve as a guiding document for demonstrating compliance with the obligations provided for in Articles 53 and 55 AI Act, while recognising that adherence to the Code does not constitute conclusive evidence of compliance with these obligations under the AI Act.

To ensure providers of general-purpose AI models comply with their obligations under the AI Act and to enable the AI Office to assess compliance of providers of general-purpose AI models who choose to rely on the Code to demonstrate compliance with their obligations under the AI Act.

enforcement_authorities: Court of Justice of the European Union
policy_extraction.penalties_summary: The Code does not set standalone monetary fines, but states that failure to verify compliance with Member States' implementation of EU copyright law before carrying out copyright-relevant acts may give rise to liability under EU copyright and related rights law, without affecting existing measures, remedies, and sanctions under Union and national law.
policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Voluntary Code of Practice chapter enabling Signatory providers of general-purpose AI models to demonstrate compliance with Article 53(1)(c) of the EU AI Act (complementary to Article 53(1)(d) training-content summaries). Adherence does not constitute conclusive evidence of AI Act compliance or compliance with EU copyright law (Directives 2001/29/EC, (EU) 2019/790, and 2004/48/EC). Proportionate measures account for provider size, including SMEs and startups. Operational commitments cover maintaining a unified copyright policy, lawful web-crawling (respecting paywalls and excluding piracy-listed sites via a dynamic EU list), honouring robots.txt (IETF RFC 9309) and other machine-readable rights reservations, mitigating copyright-infringing outputs (with tailored documentation rules for free and open-source models), and maintaining a rightsholder point of contact and electronic complaint mechanism.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document's dominant framing is fundamental_rights because its overarching objective anchors governance in fundamental rights enshrined in the EU Charter and the rule of law, and the entire substantive chapter is justified around protecting the exclusive legal rights of rightsholders under Union copyright law, respecting reservations of rights, and preserving legal remedies and complaint mechanisms. Innovation_enablement is a secondary frame, reflected in the preamble's goal of promoting the uptake of trustworthy AI and supporting innovation, as well as the recital emphasizing proportionate measures tailored to SMEs and startups. Fundamental_rights edges out innovation_enablement because every operative commitment is structured around safeguarding rightsholders' statutory rights rather than reducing compliance friction. Health and safety (consumer_public_safety) and internal market functioning (economic_competitiveness) appear only briefly as inherited Article 1(1) AI Act boilerplate in the preamble.

evidence_spans.quote: ensuring a high level of protection of health, safety, and fundamental rights enshrined in the Charter, including democracy, the rule of law, and environmental protection, against harmful effects of AI in the Union, and to support innovation pursuant to Article 1(1) AI Act.

This Chapter aims to contribute to the proper application of the obligation laid down in Article 53(1), point (c), of the AI Act pursuant to which providers that place general-purpose AI models on the Union market must put in place a policy to comply with Union law on copyright and related rights
The overarching objective of this Code of Practice (“Code”) is to improve the functioning of the internal market, to promote the uptake of human-centric and trustworthy artificial intelligence (“AI”)
The commitments in this Chapter that require proportionate measures should be commensurate and proportionate to the size of providers, taking due account of the interests of SMEs, including startups.
